question: The shadow of a tower becomes 60 m longer when the altitude of the sun changes from 45° to 30°. The height of the tower is:

question: The angles of elevation of a balloon from two consecutive kilometre-stones along a road are 30° and 60°. The height of the balloon above the ground is:
independent_reasoning: The two stones are 1 km apart: h√3 − h/√3 = 1 ⇒ 2h/√3 = 1 ⇒ h = √3/2 km.

question: There are two temples on the two banks of a river just opposite to each other. One temple is 54 m high. From the top of this temple, the angles of depression of the top and the foot of the other temple are 30° and 60° respectively. The height of the other temple is:
independent_reasoning: River width = 54/√3 = 18√3. Drop to the other temple's top = 18√3·tan30° = 18, so its height = 54 − 18 = 36 m.

question: A vertical pole and a vertical tower stand on the same level ground. The pole is 10 m high. From the top of the pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60° and the angle of depression of the foot of the tower is 30°. The height of the tower is:
independent_reasoning: Horizontal gap = 10/tan30° = 10√3. Rise above the pole = 10√3·tan60° = 30, so the tower = 10 + 30 = 40 m.

question: A vertical post 15 ft high is broken at a certain height and its upper part, not completely separated, meets the ground at an angle of 30°. The height at which the post is broken is:
independent_reasoning: With broken height h and upper part 15 − h, sin30° = h/(15 − h) = 1/2 ⇒ 2h = 15 − h ⇒ h = 5 ft.

question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from the bottom of a building is twice that from its top. If the tower is 75 m high and the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the bottom of the building is 60°, the height of the building is:
independent_reasoning: Horizontal gap = 75/√3 = 25√3; from the building top tan30° = (75 − h)/(25√3) ⇒ 75 − h = 25 ⇒ h = 50 m.

question: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points on the ground at distances a and b from its base, in the same straight line with the tower, are complementary. The height of the tower is:
independent_reasoning: For complementary angles (h/a)(h/b) = tanθ·cotθ = 1, so h² = ab and h = √(ab).

question: An aeroplane flying at a height of 5000 m passes vertically above another aeroplane, when the angles of elevation of the two aeroplanes from the same point on the ground are 60° and 45° respectively. The vertical distance between the aeroplanes at that instant is:
independent_reasoning: Horizontal distance = 5000/√3; the lower plane is 5000/√3 high (tan45° = 1), so the gap = 5000 − 5000/√3 = 5000(1−1/√3) m.

question: At the foot of a mountain the elevation of its summit is 45°. After ascending 3 km towards the mountain up a slope of 30° inclination, the elevation is found to be 60°. The height of the mountain is:
independent_reasoning: Ascending 3 km at 30°: horizontal 3√3/2, vertical 3/2. Then h − 3/2 = √3(h − 3√3/2) ⇒ h(√3−1) = 3 ⇒ h = (3/2)(√3+1) km.

question: A tower standing on a horizontal plane subtends a certain angle at a point 160 m from its foot. On advancing 100 m towards it, the tower subtends an angle twice as before. The height of the tower is:
independent_reasoning: tanθ = h/160, tan2θ = h/60. Using tan2θ = 2tanθ/(1−tan²θ): (8/3)t = 2t/(1−t²) ⇒ t² = 1/4 ⇒ h = 160/2 = 80 m.
source: _Height and Distance 02_.pdf, PDF page 16; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

question: A round balloon of radius r subtends an angle α at the eye of an observer, while the angle of elevation of its centre is β. The height of its centre above the horizontal is:
independent_reasoning: Distance to the centre = r·cosec(α/2); the centre's height = that distance × sinβ = r·sinβ·cosec(α/2).

question: From a point P, the tangent of the angle of elevation of a tower is 3/4. On walking 560 m towards the tower, the tangent of the angle of elevation becomes 4/3. The height of the tower is:
independent_reasoning: Base distances are 4h/3 and 3h/4; 4h/3 − 3h/4 = 560 ⇒ 7h/12 = 560 ⇒ h = 960 m.
